correctness.rationale: For each real continuous edgewise-W1,1 function on a finite unit metric tree, the edge derivative identifies the quotient by constants isometrically with L1 on all edges. The volume-centered all-leaf trace kernel at a cut has r entries 1-a/N and q entries -a/N, giving Q(a); strict convexity on each edge proves the finite endpoint-cut norm. When both cut components have edges, r<=s and q<=N-s-1; isolated-leaf cuts contribute <=1. The resulting concave integer quadratic Phi_N has unique maximum at floor(N/2) for N>=4. Its equality forces both components to be stars. All threshold, parity, and nonattainment cases are derived analytically, with 325330 exact arithmetic diagnostics for finite samples; diagnostics are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Euclidean leaf trace for network signals with a bounded total-gradient budget and a fixed volume mean is a natural endpoint embedding operator. Its sharp cut law is computable for arbitrary trees; all-tree optimization proves the first amplification at five edges, unique balanced-double-star worst topology for each larger size, growth C_N~sqrt(N)/2, and lack of Sobolev norm attainment. This contrasts structurally with known L2-energy point-evaluation star/path extremizers, giving a nontrivial topology-sensitive trace phenomenon rather than an arbitrary finite constant.
